notes.title: Blue Magic Cards: Mobility - Part 1
notes.notes:
This week we’ll be diving into a few of the Magic Cards you’ll have at your disposal as you make your way through Lele’s Palace. As mentioned previously in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/newshub/app/1037130/view/2949254749587110922][b]Introduction to Magic Cards[/b][/url], Dandy Ace’s core mechanic revolves around the Magical Cards which act as skills in the game. Players are able to create countless combinations of skills, upgrades, and play styles by combining the different cards they come across on each run. 

[previewyoutube=VptDygi3xUc;full][/previewyoutube]

We can not begin talking about Blue Cards without mentioning the two main types of mobility skills found in Dandy Ace; [b]Blinks[/b] & [b]Dashes[/b]. Nothing will get you through the palace quicker than the wide variety blinks, dashes, and other mobility based skills that make up the Blue Magic Cards. [b]Dashes[/b] allow Ace to travel forward and pass through enemies but do not offer any invulnerability frames during the dash. Ace is vulnerable to enemies and can’t dash through attacks without taking damage. [b]Blinks[/b] on the other hand allow Ace to teleport forward a short distance, avoiding any enemy attacks that may be between the start and end points.

While these skills let you move between enemies and around obstacles, they can also bring a lot of utility as well as additional offensive options during combat. 

[h2][b]Dashing Dash[/b][/h2]
[code]                       [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/fb87c87cff59bfa708c1a85c7050a92cfd02948b.png[/img] 
       [/code]
Starting off with dashes, the most basic Blue Card you’ll come across in Dandy Ace is [b]Dashing Dash[/b]. Using [b]Dashing Dash[/b] will have Ace dash forward dealing damage to anything in his path. Ace is able to travel through enemies during the dash dealing the full damage to each enemy hit. As mentioned previously, Ace will need to be careful though when dashing towards enemies due to [b]Dashing Dash[/b] not having any invulnerability frames.

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/gTQH5mQ/dd1.gif[/img][/url]

One of the strongest aspects of [b]Dashing Dash[/b] is its Upgrade Effect which adds [b]Haste (Buff)[/b] to any card it is combined with. If a card is activated while upgraded with [b]Dashing Dash[/b], Ace will gain [b]Haste[/b] for a short period of time increasing Ace’s movement speed by 50%. Some Upgrade Effects, such as [b]Haste[/b], will have internal cooldowns. While the Upgrade Effect is on cooldown you may still activate the base card but will not receive the additional upgraded bonuses. Any cooldowns for cards used as upgrades can be seen below the base skills on your action bar when activated. 


[b][h2]Blazing Sprint[/h2][/b]
[code]                      [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/4139f200562d4e07e3dd035bd15bdc4c21f3d872.png[/img]
       [/code]
Light your path ablaze with Dandy Ace’s [b]Blazing Sprint[/b] Card. When activated Ace will dash forward, leaving a trail of blue fire behind him for a short period of time. Any enemy that Ace dashes through takes a small amount of damage. While the initial damage may be weaker than that of [b]Dashing Dance[/b], the fire will continue to deal damage to any enemies that remain in it. This can be useful when attempting to kite groups of enemies around obstacles or immobile enemies such as Totems that are unable to avoid the blue flames.

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/P5JSCrV/bs1.gif[/img][/url]

Looking for a different Magic Card but really like the trail of blue fire? Use [b]Blazing Sprint[/b] to upgrade another card with [b]Blazing Shoes (Buff)[/b]. When the upgraded skill is upgraded, Ace will start leaving a trail of blue fire behind him for a short period of time. [b]Blazing Shoes[/b] allows Ace to move around freely and lay out the trail of fire in a more strategic way rather than in a straight line when dashing. The other benefit of [b]Blazing Shoes[/b] is the amount of area you are able to cover while it's active. 


[h2][b]Shocking Arrival[/b][/h2]
[code]                      [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/5f3ded99e640deb5c47671e29e6532f107d4d11a.png[/img] 
       [/code]
Another dash in Ace’s arsenal, [b]Shocking Arrival[/b], will specifically punish mobile enemies looking to chase after or run from Ace. When activated Ace will dash forward, creating an explosion at the end of the dash that deals damage to anyone within range. Any enemies hit by [b]Shocking Arrival[/b] will also gain a [b]Hex (Debuff)[/b] during which the affected enemies take damage while moving.

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/QJBPF1k/Hex1.gif[/img][/url]

If you choose to instead upgrade another card with [b]Shocking Arrival[/b], that card will gain the [b]Hex (Debuff)[/b] effect that is applied to enemies on hit. This can often be a very powerful tool when combined with Pink Cards and skills that can hit multiple targets quickly. It is important to note that [b]Hex [/b]will only deal damage if the enemy moves while they have the [b]Hex[/b] debuff. This makes it ineffective against Totems and Turrets but can be paired with knockbacks, pushes, and other displacement skills to maximize Ace’s damage when using [b]Shocking Arrival[/b]. 

[h2][b]Jump Scare[/b][/h2]
[code]                      [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/725b14d0a5e150b430d7b473ab0c9365caabc0f3.png[/img]
       [/code]
One of the more unique blink based Blue Cards available to Ace is [b]Jump Scare[/b]. Activating [b]Jump Scare[/b] blinks you forward, dealing damage to and scaring away any enemies within range. [b]Fear (CC) [/b]is applied to all enemies hit causing them to move away from Ace and restricts their attacks for a very short period of time. 

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/b1MKmsW/jumpscare1.gif[/img][/url]

The Upgrade Effect will vary depending on the color of the Magic Card [b]Jump Scare[/b] upgrades. [b]Fear (CC)[/b] is added to Yellow and Blue cards. [b]Taste of Fear[/b] is added to Pink cards. [b]Taste of Fear[/b] causes any enemies affected by [b]Fear[/b] to take additional damage from the upgraded skill.

[h2][b]Resonance Cascade[/b][/h2]
[code]                      [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/985fbe394c2318b43095939f4b3869ca0ad36b51.png[/img] 
       [/code]
Travel back and forth between portals when you use [b]Resonance Cascade[/b]. When used, Ace blinks forward and opens two portals. The portals are located at the initial location [b]Resonance Cascade[/b] is activated and the end point Ace blinks to. For a short period of time, Ace will be able to travel between the portals. Damage is dealt to any enemies near the portals every time Ace travels through them. 

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/7VJHYdH/p1.gif[/img][/url]

If you’re constantly dealing with multiple enemies surrounding you, consider using [b]Resonance Cascade[/b] to upgrade another card. The upgraded card will gain [b]Dimensional Burst[/b] which causes Ace to deal damage to all nearby enemies when the upgraded skill is activated.

notes.title: Welcome to the Art Gallery: Art Apprentice & Axolangelo
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=Z-LbBr7sXNA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]ART GALLERY[/h2]
The next level in our Map and Enemy spotlight series is the [b]Art Gallery[/b]! Home to Dandy Ace’s first boss [b]Axolangelo, the Master of the Arts[/b], and his [b]Art Apprentices[/b]. Take a look around at the showcased museum assets, paintings, and sculptures found within Axolangelo’s Art Gallery but don’t stare too long and most importantly.... [b]DO NOT TOUCH![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/67d81c2d5fab09478627a315e5ff6d371539534a.png[/img]

The [b]Art Gallery[/b] comes after the [b]Entrance Hall[/b] and [b]Banquet Hall[/b] levels if Ace chooses to continue down that path. Players can expect the difficulty to begin to ramp up upon entry into the Art Gallery leading up to [b]Axolangelo’s Atelier[/b], where you’ll take on Axolangelo himself. Cuckoo Nightmares, Totems, Midnight Phantoms, Art Apprentices, and Bunny Butlers & Jesters stand guard over the valuable pieces of art Ace will have to maneuver around while avoiding attacks. 

Ace will also need to watch his step as the ground is littered with one of the first environmental hazards found in Dandy Ace, [b]Spike Traps[/b]. After stepping onto the trap and a short delay, the trap will activate dealing damage to anyone found on top of it. Ace is able to utilize the traps himself by luring or knocking enemies onto them to deal a good chunk of damage. It's always important to be careful where you blink and dash to!

[h2]ART APPRENTICE[/h2]
[code]                       [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/b66662064a06012284163266b1c16e2a1da31767.gif[/img] 
       [/code]
A somewhat miniature version of Axolangelo, the [b]Art Apprentice[/b] utilizes it’s art skills to battle against Ace. The Art Apprentice is easily recognizable by its weapon of choice, its trusty giant paintbrush. While the paintbrush may not look too dangerous up close, it excels in ranged combat by covering large areas in waves of paint. 

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/5MqTf0C/Art-Apprentice-Wave.gif[/img][/url]

When at range the [b]Art Apprentice[/b] will swing his giant paintbrush sending a blue [b]Paint Wave[/b] that expands over time as it travels. The wave begins fairly small but quickly grows to cover entire pathways and larger parts of the level so Ace will need to quickly move out of the way or run quite a ways back to avoid taking hits. The real difficulty comes in when attempting to avoid several waves coming at Ace at once from multiple Art Apprentices at different ranges as the waves will vary in size. Similar to the [b]Bunny Jester[/b] discussed previously, the Art Apprentice will [b]Tumble[/b] away if Ace manages to get too close before continuing to send out additional [b]Paint Wave[/b] attacks from range.

[h2]AXOLANGELO[/h2]
[code]                       [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/cec874c396efe639727b5f3abe9da429c3189a47.gif[/img]
       [/code]

Once you find your way through the Art Gallery, you’ll stumble upon Dandy Ace’s first Boss in [b]Axolangelo’s Atelier[/b]. The development team wanted to lean into the artist stereotypes when creating a boss centered around the Art Gallery and really liked the Axolotl animal. By combining the Axolotl with famous artist Michelangelo the team was able to create [b]Axolangelo, the Master of the Arts! [/b]With a paintbrush in his hand and an art apron around his neck, Axolangelo is ready to unleash his art skills to kick Ace out of the Art Gallery. 

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/gj3yTx7/Axolangelo-Start.gif[/img][/url]

With a wide range of paint based attacks, [b]Axolangelo[/b] will have the player constantly on the move trying to avoid them. Axolangelo’s most basic of attack’s is his [b]Brush Stroke[/b]. If within range, Axolangelo will attempt to swing at Ace in an AoE cone in front of him. The area will remain covered in paint for a short period of time dealing damage to Ace if stepped on. Similar to that of the [b]Art Apprentice[/b] but bigger, [b]Axolangelo[/b] is able to send out a large [b]Paint Wave[/b] that expands over time as it travels to prevent Ace from remaining at range safely.

The Atelier is a large open space so Axolangelo has to cover areas of the level in paint from above to restrict Ace’s movement options. Axolangelo relocates himself to the center of his Atelier after which he begins to rain [b]Paint Drops[/b] down on top of Ace’s current position one by one. Upon landing the area will remain covered in paint for a period of time dealing damage to Ace if stepped on. Axolangelo will also periodically surround himself with [b]Painter’s Aura[/b] damaging anything he is able to get close enough to as he chases Ace.

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/8bC6jWZ/Axolangelo1.gif[/img][/url]

While Axolangelo may be big, he sure can move! If you manage to anger Axolangelo he’ll start looking to charge at Ace utilizing his [b]Paint Rush[/b]. Ace will have a short opening to move out of the way before [b]Axolangelo[/b] charges in a straight line, dealing damage and carrying Ace if caught in its path. The combination of these skills creates an exciting and challenging experience that will leave players experimenting with different builds before being able to efficiently and consistently take him on!

[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/p44dRHp/Axolangelo-2.gif[/img][/url]

If you’d like to visit the [b]Art Gallery[/b] to take on [b]Axolangelo[/b] and his [b]Art Apprentices[/b] you can do so today by downloading our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1037130/Dandy_Ace/][b]Free Demo[/b][/url] available on the[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1037130/Dandy_Ace/][b] Dandy Ace Steam Page[/b][/url]! If you haven’t already done so, please consider helping us out by adding Dandy Ace to your Steam Wishlist. Tune into next week’s spotlight as we dive deeper into some of the Magic Cards you’ll come across in Dandy Ace.

notes.title: Introduction to Dandy Ace's Magic Cards
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/68d700cc25140bc0894a377fee547e1642bfa3df.jpg[/img]
One of the most important and core mechanics in Dandy Ace revolves around the Magic Cards which act as the skills in the game. Players can create countless combinations of skills, upgrades, and playstyles by combining the different cards they come across. Additional Cards can be earned through multiple ways during your playthrough such as by defeating groups of enemies, picking up Card Blueprints, using Shards at the Reward Tent, and purchasing them with gold at Shops you find. Ace will begin each run with access to one Blue Card, one Pink Card, and one Yellow Card randomly selected from the starting pool.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/807d2c06546ab862df14a05235e70bf0f3856b2e.png[/img]

Every Magical Card has a default skill associated with it. These skills can be upgraded further by combining Magical Cards together to change how the skills function and/or provide additional utility or damage potential to a skill. There are more than a thousand possibilities for you to play with!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/d34d4c7349b8f4de76eefa09640b881578c06ce2.png[/img]

Players are also able to find stronger versions of each card as they progress through the maps and experiment with different skills. The Tiers of a Magic Card will impact things like cooldown time and the damage of a card’s base skill effects but not its effects when utilized as an upgrade to be combined with another card. Upgrade effects can only be impacted by the Tier of the base card it is being combined with. Tooltips will be available in-game to explain to players what each type of Buff, Debuff, and Skill does as well as how a card will affect another when it is used as an upgrade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/67fc7c39e6627ab3ea02dd7f37ce22c9c2e96a91.jpg[/img]

It is important to note that players are not guaranteed the same cards each run so it will be important to learn them all! We feel like we have done a pretty good job so far of creating viable skill effects for each Magic Card so that players can utilize different combinations that not only suit their own playstyles, but also create interesting combat scenarios between different runs and against each type of enemy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/b439bc59467bb26cccbb41d63b3687847e8cc94f.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Blue Cards function as the Movement based skills. These are split into two main categories: Dashes and Blinks. 
[/list]
[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/tY62DGL/ca2161d6c330048d6e12b86a24ebe2f0-original.gif[/img][/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/ced9b145ad70f6f047edc93e9926184cf458da09.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Pink Cards are the more damage oriented cards, split into Melee and Ranged skills.
[/list]
[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/nLQ7MD4/f01308f127f45d19a7db96719d04d173-original.gif[/img][/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/da00a53c5c3c9573aaa0315b470783c66a2b5286.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Yellow Cards have the widest variety of mechanics associated with them. The skills can range from giant barriers & personal shields to slow fields and stuns.
[/list]
[url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/b2wQmhK/90c647ba2b1fcc6f2f785248d2cfea72-original.gif[/img][/url]

That about covers all of the basics for the Magic Cards in Dandy Ace. Make sure to hop in during our Challenge Event that is currently ongoing until Saturday, October 24th. The Challenge Event features lots of new Magic Cards to experiment with as well as enemies that were not previously available in the Demo or our first Beta test. notes.title: Welcome to the Entrance Hall: Bunny Butler, Bunny Jester, & Cuckoo Nightmare
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/c5e09e0d99bec83601aa4630839bf09b86187f20.png[/img]

[previewyoutube=n_vrs4zwmhs;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]ENTRANCE HALL[/h2]
Starting today, we’re going to begin slowly introducing you to the maps, characters, and enemies you’ll come across in Dandy Ace as you make your way through the Cursed Mirror! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/bef4c580b93d2239cc7e1f3112b4d583ed4b360e.png[/img]

You’ll begin your journey into Lele’s Palace in the [b]Entrance Hall[/b], the first and shortest map in Dandy Ace. This map is home to the most common and basic enemies, easing you into the challenges you’ll face later on. After being trapped in the Cursed Mirror, Ace will pick up his initial Magic Cards as well as have his first encounter with [b]Lele, the Green-Eyed Illusionist[/b], here at the start of the [b]Entrance Hall[/b]. Depending on the keys Ace has acquired, he will also gain access to numerous paths in the [b]Entrance Hall[/b] leading to other maps such as the[b] Banquet Hall[/b] or [b]Art Gallery[/b]. Depending on how often you are defeated, there is a chance you'll get to know the Entrance Hall and its inhabitants very well although the layout of the maps does change with the start of each new run providing you with a slightly different experience.

[h2]BUNNY BUTLER & BUNNY JESTER[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/f4912f856ab22f1153cb3db1c04ccde538652873.png[/img]

The first enemies Ace encounters are the [b]Bunny Butler [/b]& [b]Bunny Jester[/b]. These are the most basic enemies in Dandy Ace but this does not mean they are to be taken lightly! As a melee based enemy the [b]Bunny Butler[/b] looks to get close to Ace whereas the [b]Bunny Jester[/b] attacks from range. The team chose the bunny because of the stereotype of performing magicians often utilizing bunnies in their tricks.

[h3]Bunny Butler[/h3]
[code]                        [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/e21b12494ff248708ecea641d0ecd2edcd9d7857.gif[/img]   
       [/code]

This is the most common enemy in Dandy Ace and players can often come across them spawning in groups in the Entrance Hall. Being a simple and straightforward enemy meant to introduce players to the combat in Dandy Ace, the Bunny Butler has one offensive ability and no defensive abilities. The Bunny Butler’s weapon of choice is a giant fork which he uses to poke at Ace. Once within range, the Bunny Butler will prepare to Charge at Ace. After a short delay he will lunge quickly in Ace’s direction dealing a significant amount of damage if you stay in its path.

[h3]Bunny Jester[/h3]
[code]                        [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/3e42764b1a643139bd4607cbee7e2f91abbae164.gif[/img]   
       [/code]                                                                                                   

A variation of the Bunny Butler, the Bunny Jester relies on ranged attacks when taking on Ace. Although still a fairly straightforward enemy, the Bunny Jester’s kit features both an offensive and defensive ability that Ace will have to play around. Capable of dodging Ace’s attacks if he gets too close, Ace will need to quickly close the distance while also utilizing his own ranged attacks to bring the Bunny Jester down. The Bunny Jester utilizes its [b]Throw[/b] ranged ability to continuously lob projectiles in Ace’s direction. However, if Ace gets too close to him, the Bunny Jester dashes away using [b]Tumble[/b] before resuming its attacks.

[h2]CUCKOO NIGHTMARE[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/01b697af1148f4b1b2ab9cdde2b7e335bf29c380.png[/img]

Heavily inspired by Alice in Wonderland, like many of the other enemies found within Dandy Ace, the Cuckoo Nightmare is players’ first taste of a more challenging enemy. A cuckoo clock with legs and teeth, the Cuckoo Nightmare is a tank with a higher HP pool and multiple offensive attacks for both up close and ranged encounters.

[h3]Cuckoo Nightmare[/h3]
[code]                         [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34727433/8eafbb3fde64fda6977b1b2b28897765b6aa8b47.gif[/img]
          [/code]

Be careful when getting close to the Cuckoo Nightmare as its teeth are not just for show! The Cuckoo Nightmare’s [b]Bite[/b] attack will deal a heavy amount of damage to Ace if you are found within biting distance. Meanwhile, if you remain at range for an extended period of time the Cuckoo Nightmare will utilize [b]Crazy Cuckoo[/b] which will send a wave of damage out towards the player before it continues to advance towards Ace. 

        [url=https://imgbb.com/][img]https://i.ibb.co/y5r1j4j/ezgif-7-618f14b8214c.gif[/img][/url]

That about covers the Entrance Hall and what players can expect to run into at the start of each playthrough. Later this month we'll be covering the [b]Art Gallery[/b] next as well as our first boss [b]Axolangelo[/b] so be sure to follow Dandy Ace on all our Social Media below. notes.title: Dandy Ace 0.0.9.0.4 Update
notes.notes:
In this patch we added a lot of new features such as Twitch Mode, Narration and Game Records! We used some of the community suggestions to help improve aspects like UI, gameplay, and visual feedback of card cooldowns and enemy behavior. We also made some changes and balance adjustments to some of the blue and yellow cards. 

[u][h2]New Features[/h2][/u]
[h3]Twitch Mode (Content Creators Build Only)[/h3]
Twitch Integration is a feature focused on streamers, giving them a lot of room and tools for direct interactions with their audiences. It allows them to play the game in a unique way that can only be experienced while streaming the game.

The chat of the streamer can interact with the game through:
[list]
[*] [b]Lele Mode[/b]: One viewer is picked from the chat, being granted the power to control Lele. This  allows them to use skills, spells and spawn enemies.
[*] [b]All Chat Interactions[/b]: During the streamer’s run, there will be many interactions that Twitch chat can vote on to decide what will happen in the game. Like deciding which kind of card the streamer will receive as reward and which level they should go to next.
[/list]
[h3]Narrator[/h3]
Throughout the game, Lele will comment on Ace's actions and interact with him through a wide variety of voice lines.

[h3]Dialogues[/h3]
We added a new dialogue system with all of the NPCs, bosses and tutorials. In addition to some new UI for it, now all of the characters have their own unique art and voices.

[h3]Game Records[/h3]
We added an interactable mirror at the entrance to each level. With it, players can check their:
[list]
[*] [b]Unlockable information:[/b] Most used cards, trinkets and permanent upgrades. As well as which items the player has already unlocked. 
[*] [b]Progression information:[/b] How many times they died, beat the game and their best times on each level.
[*] [b]Enemy information:[/b] How many times the player has killed or been killed by each enemy.
[/list]
[h3](Community Suggestion) Cooldown Feedback[/h3]
We heard players complain about not really knowing when their skills are off cooldown and having to look at their skill bar, averting their focus from the gameplay, and potentially putting them in danger while doing so. To help with this issue, we implemented the following changes based on feedback regarding skill cooldowns:
[list]
[*] Yellow Card's icons briefly appear above Ace when the skill gets off cooldown.
[*] Added visual feedback on all cards to show when a card is still on cooldown (on skill bar HUD).
[*] Added visual feedback on all cards to show when a card gets off cooldown (on skill bar HUD).
[*] Added audio feedback on cards with longer cooldown to indicate when a card is still on cooldown.
[/list]
[h3]Tooltip System[/h3]
We noticed some important mechanics of the game weren’t being easily understood and used as quickly as we wanted players to use them. To help players understand them a bit better, we added a simple tooltip system that is triggered when cards are equipped in a certain order.

[u][h2]Changes & Balancing[/h2][/u]
[h3]Blue Cards[/h3]
- Reduced all of the dash and blink cooldowns and adjusted the damage accordingly.

[h3]Yellow Cards[/h3]
- Reduced the overall cooldown of Yellow Cards and adjusted the damage accordingly.

[h3]Difficulty[/h3]
[b](Community Feedback) Entrance Hall reduction:[/b] We heard a lot of new players talking about the length of the first level and that it took longer than it should. We agreed that as an introductory level it didn’t need to be that long. So we removed some rooms and rearranged the map  to make it shorter. 

[b]Cupcake drop:[/b] On every level, cupcakes would drop 2 to 3 times. We have increased the drop rate to make sure that 3 cupcakes will spawn on each level.

[b](Community Feedback) Initial Pink Card:[/b] We felt that for new players the constant change in skills for their first few attempts could be a bit too difficult. To improve that we made the starter pink card always be Five of a Kind (similarly with how the start blue card is always Dashing Dash). Once players get to the Banquet Hall for the first time, they can unlock a cheap upgrade that will expand the number of starter pink cards the player can receive.

[b](Community Feedback) Card Gold Prices:[/b] We updated the shop’s Card prices, making them more accessible.

[h3](Community Feedback) Enemy Attack Feedback[/h3]
We improved the feedback that indicates when an enemy will be making an attack. This makes it a lot easier to predict and react to the various attacks enemies have. To get to this result we did a few things: 
[list]
[*] Enemies grow bigger before attacking
[*] Enemies glow in white for longer before attacking
[*] Floating Damage numbers from Ace’s attacks were made a bit smaller and spread out more to make it easier for players to see the enemies while damaging them
[*] Now there is no overlap between feedback on enemies. Before this change, enemies would glow in white before attacking, but would get overlapped by a red glow when they got hit by Ace
[/list]
[b]And we addressed and fixed several bugs[/b]

notes.title: Dandy Ace postpone release date
notes.notes:
The most important factor for this decision was our commitment to quality, in addition to the extremely positive feedback from the community.

Among the additions and improvements prepared for Dandy Ace in this extension of development we can expect:

[b]A new game mode[/b] - An ambitious new mode that transforms Dandy Ace's gameplay will be added to the game as originally planned

[b]Narrative Improvements[/b] - Addition of new dialogues and narration of characters within the game

[b]Twitch Integration[/b] - Spectators will be able to interact with streamers when playing

[b]Game Records[/b] - General performance statistics will be recorded so that players can check their best times on a run, which card is most used, which was their most dangerous enemy, number of hours of play and much more

[b]New enemies[/b] - Creation of at least 5 new original enemies

We're very sorry for this postpone, but is for a good reason. Until then, you can try a playable demo version of Dandy Ace available on Steam!
